messages:
aly_support: Customer reported a burst of 502s hitting /v1/generate around 09:12 UTC. They said it started after a batch job sent ~600 parallel requests with ~4-6k token prompts. They included one trace-id: trace=edg-9f4a. Happening for ~30m and is ongoing. Customer URL + example: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate :eyes:

aly_support: Quick repro they gave (they say only happens at scale):
```bash
for i in {1..600}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -d '{"model":"open-llama-70b","input":"'""Long prompt..."'"','"max_tokens":1024}' \
       https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\ndone; wait
```

incidents-bot: alert: edge.gateway.5xx spike detected (09:13 UTC) — 502/504 rate increased to 4.7% over baseline. Linked dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/edge-5xx-spike :chart_with_upwards_trend:

tony_sre: grabbing traces now. initial hunch: connection pool / stream exhaustion at the edge proxy. Can @kevin_eng pull envoy metrics for the hosts serving the hosted-api pool? :mag:

kevin_eng: on it. looking at envoy_cluster_stats for cluster hosted-api-upstream. seeing `rq_2xx` low, `rq_5xx` high, `upstream_cx_idle_timeout` spikes, and `upstream_failures` bumping. Also `downstream_rq_active` is maxing on some nodes.

maria_ops: seeing a subset of nodes with high `http2.active_streams` close to 1000 concurrent streams, others normal. Looks like client-side bursts are unevenly routed. Might be uneven load balancing on frontdoor.

aly_support: customer attached sample response headers from a 502: `x-edge-trace: edg-9f4a`, `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 0`, `via: 1.1 edge-router`, body: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers". They insisted upstream returned nothing.

tony_sre: that matches pool exhaustion. Envoy will return 502 if it can't get a healthy upstream stream. Also seeing `stream reset` logs with reason `REFUSED_STREAM` and occasional `RST_STREAM`.

kevin_eng: posting quick repro we did locally to simulate their pattern (reduced):
```python
# quick stress repro (python, asyncio)
import aiohttp, asyncio
async def call(i):
  async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
    async with s.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json={"model":"open-llama-70b","input":"x"*2000}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer $KEY"}) as r:
      return r.status, await r.text()
async def main():
  tasks = [call(i) for i in range(150)]
  print(await asyncio.gather(*tasks))
asyncio.run(main())
```
Result: ~15% 502s after concurrency >120. Logs on edge show repeated `upstream reset` and `max concurrent streams` warnings.

aly_support: customer asked if this is related to auth service or billing header injection we rolled last week. They reported they didn’t see auth failures in their logs.

tony_sre: validated: no 401s or auth errors in our traces tied to those trace ids. Upstream auth calls are healthy. This looks like pure connection saturation at proxy layer.

kevin_eng: short-term mitigations we can try:
- increase per-host `max_concurrent_streams` setting on edge-router cluster or add additional upstream hosts to spread connections.
- enable connection pooling tweaks: `http2.max_concurrent_streams` bump and `idle_timeout` tuning.
- apply per-connection circuit breaker changes to avoid single-host hot spots.

maria_ops: also recommend throttling at the ingress gateway for very large batch concurrency until a permanent fix. Can we push a temporary Envoy config change?

deploy-bot: deploy request opened by @tony_sre: `edge-config/tweak-http2-streams` (PR #4531). Canary to 5% first.

kevin_eng: running canary now. if metrics look good, we roll to 50% in 15m.

aly_support: what should I tell the customer now? they’re asking for an immediate workaround.

tony_sre: reply with: 1) we’re actively mitigating (canary rolling now), 2) ask them to reduce parallelism to <=100 as workaround, 3) provide backoff/retry guidance (exponential backoff with jitter) and 4) we can route high-concurrency jobs to Dedicated/reserved pool for predictable throughput. Keep them updated in 10m. :thumbsup:

kevin_eng: can we also surface a client-side SDK recommendation: stream smaller requests (split prompts), reuse connections (keep-alive), add `Connection: keep-alive` and fewer parallel processes per host. That reduces head-of-line pressure.

maria_ops: monitoring: added a dashboard panel for `envoy.http2.active_streams` per node + `upstream_cx_total`. Alert threshold set to 85% of node stream capacity.

aly_support: customer replied, says they can reduce to 80 concurrent requests as a stopgap and asked for ETA.

tony_sre: ETA: 30–45min to validate canary and roll. assigning follow-up: @kevin_eng to validate metrics during roll, @maria_ops to keep dashboard/watch, support to update customer.

kevin_eng: canary metrics look promising: drop in 502s from 4.7% -> 1.2% on canary hosts. rolling to 50% now.

deploy-bot: deploy `edge-config/tweak-http2-streams` promoted to 50% (09:38 UTC).

aly_support: passing to customer: we rolled a config change to improve HTTP/2 stream handling at the edge; ask them to keep concurrency <=100 and follow backoff guidance. If they can, we also offered routing to Dedicated pool for large batch jobs.

maria_ops: follow-up action items (tickets):
- SRE-3129: investigate long-term LB fix for uneven routing/hotspot (assigned to kevin_eng).
- OPS-4132: add autoscale policy to add more upstream hosts when active_streams high (assigned to maria_ops).
- DOC-2298: client guidance on concurrency/backoff + SDK examples (assigned to eng docs).

aly_support: customer acknowledged and will test reduced concurrency. said they appreciate the quick response. closing loop after 2h monitoring. :white_check_mark:

tony_sre: markers: if 502s creep back up after roll -> revert + investigate deeper (connection-count accounting, TLS/session reuse). For now, keep an eye on `upstream_cx_overflow` and `http2.max_concurrent_streams` breach logs.

kevin_eng: added debug logging for affected edge nodes for next 2h: `envoy: debug connection limit hit` so we have richer traces if it recurs.

incidents-bot: resolved alert: edge.gateway.5xx spike mitigated (09:47 UTC).
